sense.text:
Before identifying Babylon, the class dealt with Israel first. “Who then is that faithful and wise steward”: the faithful are the faithful in Christ, and the wise are those made wise through God’s commandments.

“Whom his lord shall make ruler over his household, to give them their portion of meat in due season” is a reward. To be made ruler is rulership, and the portion of meat in due season is the kingdom: Christ is going to make us rulers over this planet.

“Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.” We want to be found blessed: in the vineyard, in the highways and hedges, teaching Israel.

When a brother says I have nothing to do, that’s a lie. The classes run seven days a week, three times a day and more; there is Clubhouse, the Isaiah 11:11 program constantly reaching out overseas to men and women, the Daughters of Sarah and Saving Sarah’s Daughters reaching out. There’s always something to do in this truth, and new things to innovate and bring to the table, for leadership to analyze spiritually and say this would be a good route to go. Brothers and sisters who say they have idle time are liars.

“He will make him ruler over all that he hath.” We are going to get the world back, brothers and sisters; we are going to rule the planet. Everybody on the planet is going to be subject to Christ, do or die, and we will be the enforcers. Your church never taught you that, because your pastor don’t know the Bible.

“My lord delayeth his coming”: the Lord ain’t coming back no time soon. To “beat the menservants” is to abuse the menservants with slander, hatred and physical violence; to beat the maidens is passing them around sexually, here and there, like Skittles. “To eat and drink, and to be drunken”: party over here. They don’t give a damn about the Commandments.

These are camps that don’t understand the Bible, and some of you were with them and still be watching these dummies. They don’t follow the Commandments at all: the first thing they do is slander Israel United in Christ. So you know they are not rolling in the spirit of the Lord, whether they call him Christ or Yahawah, Bahasham, Yahawashi. They don’t have the Holy Spirit on them.

“The lord of that servant will come in a day when he looketh not for him, and at an hour when he is not aware, and will cut him in sunder, and will appoint him his portion with the unbelievers.”

These Israelite men on the street talking about Esau going into the lake of fire: Christ says you are going to get the same judgment as the white man you call the devil. You can curse the white man out all day, but if you are breaking the Commandments, his judgment is your judgment.

“And that servant, which knew his lord’s will, and prepared not himself”: that’s some of you in here, and some of the brothers and sisters following online. They know, because they are being taught properly: keep the Commandments and the faith of Christ, over and over. Not preparing yourself is not building yourself up correctly in the spirit, not putting on the whole armour of God.

“Neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes”: you’re going to get judged. And some know the Lord’s will and still don’t prepare themselves.

“But he that knew not, and did commit things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few stripes.” Some men and women in these camps are being taught so egregiously, so wrongly, so heinously, it’s unimaginable. Don’t let the word few throw you off: you’re still getting punished.

“For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required”: this is why we don’t take rank lightly, and don’t take this Bible lightly. It’s easy to be a soldier or a member, but as you become an officer of ten, of twenty, more responsibility comes, and more is required of you. A lot of black men don’t like responsibility; households fall apart because of it. Some come here saying they want responsibility, and when it’s given everything falls apart in their hands and they act like we’re the enemy. The Lord is looking for those few men who can handle responsibility.

So study, pray, apply, and don’t waste time: rank is for the serious-minded brothers. Saving Sarah’s Daughters can’t have any old sister, a walking dummy instructing young women; it has to be a sister who studies and has a sound mind. Even the kids’ room is a responsibility: one school’s kids’ room had to be closed down. It is not a hangout spot. Don’t be on your phone laughing and joking while the children do whatever they want, because you never know what kids will do.
“I am come to send fire on the earth”: when Christ returns there’s going to be war on the planet. His second coming will be in the midst of war.

precepts.why: Faithful in what? Paul writes “to the saints which are at Ephesus, and to the faithful in Christ Jesus.” The faithful steward of Luke 12:42 is faithful in Christ Jesus.

The wise steward: “Thou through thy commandments hast made me wiser than mine enemies: for they are ever with me.” It is only through God’s commandments that we become wise, wiser than our enemies. This verse carries through the whole beginning of the lesson.

“The wise in heart will receive commandments: but a prating fool shall fall.” Only the wise in heart are going to receive the Commandments. A prating fool is a fool of lip: somebody that likes to run their mouth and slander.

When you hear brothers or sisters say to hell with the Commandments, you don’t need no Commandments, get the hell away from them. There’s a lot of Israelite camps that echo those very sentiments, and some of you might have run from them and come in here.

“Whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a wise man’s heart discerneth both time and judgment.” The wise man’s heart, his mind, discerns. “Because to every purpose there is time and judgment, therefore the misery of man is great upon him.”

When you are that wise brother, that wise sister keeping the Commandments, you are considerate of time and judgment. You are well aware when it’s time to go, when it’s time to shut up, when it’s time to move, and when judgment is about to come.

What does it mean to be made ruler over his household, to give them their portion of meat in due season? It’s a reward. Christ says, “Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.” The second came saying, “Lord, thy pound hath gained five pounds”, and to him likewise: “Be thou also over five cities.”

That is rulership. To the servant who had a little and multiplied it, be ruler over ten cities. A city is big, a city is huge: you need power, you need authority to be over a city. Christ is going to make us rulers over this planet, and that is the portion of meat in due season: the kingdom.

Ruler over all that he hath: “And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High.” Under the whole heaven is the whole planet earth. We’re going to get the world back; we’re going to rule the planet.

“Whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom”: the kingdom that’s coming is going to be everlasting. “And all dominions shall serve and obey him”: everybody’s going to be subject to Christ. Everybody on the planet, do or die, and we will be the enforcers.

“And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations.” To overcome is to overcome the sins of this world and your personal sins. To keep the works of Christ is to keep the Commandments, unto the end.

“And he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers.” We’re going to rule the nations with a rod of iron, with rigor, with austerity; we ain’t playing with nary one of them. We’re going to break the nations like a potter breaks a vessel. To break the nations we need power: some of you got a 9 millimeter, but you got 15 shots and a hundred out front. That ain’t going to work. Christ is going to give us that power.

“Even as I received of my Father”: the same blessings Christ got, he is going to give to us. Your church never taught you that, because your pastor don’t know the Bible.

“And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ.” That’s why Christ said in Revelation 2, “even as I received of my Father”: because we’re joint heirs with him. Joint heirs means what Christ gets, we get.

“If so be that we suffer with him”: we got to go through some stuff. It’s always going to be hard times; tribulation is coming, persecution is coming, and we have to endure it. That is when you’re going to be that real joint heir and get that power, “that we may be also glorified together.”

Christ speaking: “But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.” Those that say, I ain’t following no black Jesus, no black Yahawashi, the hell with that.

That’s why we’re going to be his enforcers on this earth. You read these parables and it’s all in there, but the church goes, I don’t know what that means.

His portion with the unbelievers: “Let the sinners be consumed out of the earth, and let the wicked be no more.” Who are the sinners? That’s Israelites. And the wicked is the white man. Let both be no more: it’s the same judgment. “Bless thou the Lord, O my soul. Praise ye the Lord.”

“But the wicked shall be cut off from the earth”: the wicked is Esau. “And the transgressors shall be rooted out of it”: the transgressors are you and me, if we decide to break the Commandments; you online in those funky donkey camps.

There it is again: the same judgment. The Israelite who breaks the Commandments gets his portion with the unbelievers.

Neither did according to his will. So what’s his will? “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” God’s law is his will, and God’s will is his law. Never be confused about the will of God: the servant who did not do according to his will is the one who did not keep the law.

Beaten with many stripes: “Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.”

“Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name?” Lord, we was on the streets teaching Yahawah, Bahasham, Yahawashi; and they were also cursing people out, slandering and lying on people. “And in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works?”

“And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.” Christ is going to say I never knew you, to you evil brothers out there and your simple followers, the few you got. To work iniquity is to break the Commandments.

sense.text:
Numbers don’t equal success; numbers equal progress, as Deacon Eythan said. If numbers were success, the Roman Catholic Church would be God’s success: they have billions. That’s not the success the Bible is talking about.

“Desire not a multitude of unprofitable children”: what good is it if we have thousands upon thousands of lazy, do-nothing brothers and sisters? It’s a waste of your time and our time, but most of all God’s time. “Neither delight in ungodly sons.”

“Though they multiply, rejoice not in them, except the fear of the Lord be with them.” Though your children multiply, though the congregation multiplies, don’t rejoice in that. We rejoice when we see brothers and sisters that love the Lord and fear God: then we’re on the right track.

In your personal homes, don’t rejoice in your kids if they’re ungodly, only if they fear the Lord. Likewise as a congregation, we don’t relish the big numbers unless the fear of God is on you.

“Trust not thou in their life, neither respect their multitude: for one that is just is better than a thousand.” Don’t respect the numbers. One member that is just is better than a thousand. That’s some heavy stuff.

precepts.why:
“But there are some of you that believe not. For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were that believed not, and who should betray him.” Christ was talking to his followers. The Son of God knew who didn’t believe on him; just because they were around him didn’t mean they believed.

It’s the same here. Some come in just for some booty, looking at a woman; some women are only here to get a man, and once they come together we don’t see them no more. Some come because their life is falling apart and they need the network to get a good job, and when they get the job we don’t see them no more. Good riddance. There’s a multitude of reasons.

“From that time many of his disciples went back, and walked no more with him.” He cut them so bad, and refused to explain himself, and a lot of them left. “Will ye also go away?” And Peter: “Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life.” That’s how we know the sincere brothers: through thick and thin they stick in this truth, because what is taught here you are not going to get in any other Israelite camp or church.

“And we believe and are sure that thou art that Christ, the Son of the living God.” One that is just is better than a thousand. You got to know the men that you’re around.

sense.text:
“Behold my servant, whom I uphold; mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth”: this is talking about Christ. “I have put my spirit upon him: he shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles.” Somebody hears Gentiles and thinks other races can come in. That ain’t what it’s talking about: the Gentiles are the remnant of Zebulun and Naphtali. Don’t let a Christian confuse you.

The lesson for us: never be on the street, at home, in here or anywhere arguing with folks. Don’t argue with other camps. Leave them alone.

“He shall not cry, nor lift up, nor cause his voice to be heard in the street.” Christ was not argumentative: he said what he said and walked off. That’s why when we teach something, that’s it; we’re not debating with nobody. What the Bible says is what it is.

You’re supposed to lift up your voice like a trumpet to teach, but that back-and-forth debating spirit, no, Christ wasn’t doing that. Don’t be out there arguing with people.

“A bruised reed shall he not break”: when John the Baptist was on the scene, Christ said John was not a reed shaken in the wind. Christ didn’t bruise John; he didn’t do anything against him. He supported John.

“And the smoking flax shall he not quench”: the men and women of Israel were the smoking flax. Christ didn’t quench their spirit; he encouraged them. “He shall bring forth judgment unto truth.”
“He shall not fail nor be discouraged, till he have set judgment in the earth: and the isles shall wait for his law.” A lot of Israelites are scattered on the islands.

precepts.why: Judgment to the Gentiles: “The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles.” The remnant of Zebulun and Naphtali that came back were called Gentiles. So the Gentiles Christ brings judgment to are Israelites, not other races. Don’t let a Christian confuse you.

“He shall not strive, nor cry; neither shall any man hear his voice in the streets.” Christ was not argumentative. He said what he said and he walked off; that was it.

That’s why when we teach something, that’s it. We’re not debating with nobody. What we say, the Bible says, and that’s what it is. The hell is this, sitting around arguing with folks?

This is how Christ taught: “For he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.” That’s how the brothers teach: we have the authority from the Lord. So what we say it means, that’s what it means. And if a scripture is twofold or threefold, we’re going to let you know.

“For the Son of man is as a man taking a far journey, who left his house, and gave authority to his servants.” He gave authority to his servants, and we’re his servants: the same authority Christ had, he gave us in the scriptures. Now we’re supposed to apologize because we got the understanding and you don’t? Hell no.

Those of you that watch our videos: we can tell when you answer a question whether you got it from us. Give credit to your elders all you want, put your elders back on the screen; people hear your answer and say, that’s the IUIC precept, that’s the way IUIC explains it. We know your elders’ level of understanding is very, very low.

What does it mean, a bruised reed shall he not break? Jesus began to say unto the multitudes concerning John: “What went ye out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind?” A reed shaken with the wind is an unstable person, and John was not that. “A man clothed in soft raiment? behold, they that wear soft clothing are in kings’ houses.”

“A prophet? yea, I say unto you, and more than a prophet.” John the Baptist was more than a prophet: “For this is he, of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.” John the Baptist is that messenger, and he prepared the way before Yahawah.

“Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he”, because in the kingdom of heaven we’re all going to be righteous; we’re going to have spiritual power. But there is nobody greater than John the Baptist: that’s what the Son of God is saying. And these clowns on the screen say John the Baptist was wicked and part of a fake Israelite camp. Are y’all insane? That’s why the judgment got to come.

So John was no reed shaken in the wind, and Christ did not bruise him. He supported John.

Matthew 11:10 is taken from Malachi: “Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant, whom ye delight in.” Right there, where it says the Lord, the Hebrew says Yahawah.

So this was a prophecy about the way being prepared for Yahawah. John the Baptist is the messenger who prepared the way before him, and when Yahawah came in the flesh, he took on that earthly form.

What does it mean, the smoking flax Christ shall not quench? “Quench not the Spirit.” Just like we’re instructed not to quench each other’s spirit: when you see a brother or sister trying their best in this truth, encourage that man, encourage that sister to keep pushing on. Keep studying, keep praying, keep applying.

That’s what Christ did. The men and women of Israel were the smoking flax, and he didn’t quench their spirit; he encouraged them.

sense.text:
The apostles did not argue either. “To whom we gave place by subjection, no, not for an hour.” Paul said we didn’t give subjection to these clowns for an hour; we didn’t entertain their foolishness. What was happening is that they were trying to bring Israel back to the old covenant of animal sacrifice, and Paul said I’m not hearing it, I’m not discussing that, it’s ridiculous.

We got to have that same mentality. We’re not arguing about the New Covenant either: what is there to argue about, what is there to debate about?

precepts.why:
“Jesus took bread, and blessed it, and brake it, and gave it to the disciples, and said, Take, eat; this is my body. And he took the cup, and gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, Drink ye all of it; For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.” That’s what Christ initiated. How you going to look at that and go, let’s argue about that? There’s nothing to argue about.

“I will not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom.” That’s when it’s going to be fulfilled, and that’s when grace is over. In the kingdom there’s no more, Lord, I committed adultery, I’m sorry, have mercy; Lord, I slandered this brother and that sister. No: death for you, off with your head. There’s no more grace. Your sins were washed away, but you abused that.

“And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament”: Christ is the mediator of the New Testament, “that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.” Who was under the first testament, the Philistines? No, the Israelites.

“For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator.” In order for a testament to be of strength, you have to die. “For a testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth.” You write a will while you’re alive: this to your wife, this to your son, your daughter, your brother, your sister, your mom. If your mama, your sister or your wife pisses you off, you can change it; it has no force while you’re alive. But once you are dead, the will is in full effect.

So was Christ crucified and did he die? Yes. So the New Testament is in force. Hope nobody’s confused and looking for a goat to go sacrifice, you big dummies.

Watch what Christ made us: “Who also hath made us able ministers of the new testament.” Did it say Old Testament? No: we are ministers, teachers, of the New Testament. “Not of the letter”: that’s the old covenant. “But of the spirit”: the spirit in Christ, the New Testament. “For the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life”: the old covenant killeth, but the New Testament gives life.

So this must be your mentality: I only debate my equals; all others I teach. Arguing with idiots is like playing chess with a pigeon: no matter how good you are, the bird is going to strut around like it won. You cut a man up in the scriptures and his whole crowd of dummies still supports him, and you just wasted your time. Leave them people alone. Don’t focus on proving people wrong; focus on the people who believe in God.

sense.text: Somebody’s saying right now, we’re supposed to debate. “Behold, ye fast for strife and debate, and to smite with the fist of wickedness”: this is in the negative, like those clowns on the screen. “Ye shall not fast as ye do this day, to make your voice to be heard on high”, because they were always arguing, always debating.

precepts.why:
“Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers.” Do y’all see that? Debate is one of the works of the flesh.

Years ago Bishop Nathanyel, Bishop Kai and Captain Zakar went to a Christian college, and they tried to lock them into one topic, the blood of Jesus, fifteen minutes and you can’t go outside of the topic. I ain’t following the stupid little rules you got; it’s foolishness. They tore their behinds up anyway, and people did repent and come out of that.

“For I fear, lest, when I come, I shall not find you such as I would, and that I shall be found unto you such as ye would not: lest there be debates.” Paul said I don’t want to come and there’s debating among you: that’s not the spirit of Christ. “Envyings, wraths, strifes, backbitings, whisperings, swellings, tumults”: the Lord don’t deal with those spirits, men that like to debate, debate, debate.

Who has understanding on this? We just read about no debating, and now it says “Debate thy cause with thy neighbour himself.” Two brothers came to the mic and both were correct: it is between each other, when you have an issue with your brother.

Here’s the key: “and discover not a secret to another.” It’s the issue between me and you, so whatever it is, I ain’t got to run to him and tell him what it is, because me and you handled it.

Somebody might try to use Acts 19. Paul “went into the synagogue, and spake boldly for the space of three months, disputing and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God. But when divers were hardened, and believed not, but spake evil of that way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus.”

That disputing didn’t mean arguing back and forth. The other translations put it as discussions, and reasoning daily, in the lecture hall of Tyrannus. And when they were hardened and spoke evil of the way, Paul left them and took the disciples with him.

And there’s an open challenge to all the camps that say they’re righteous before the Lord: travel to another country where we’re not teaching, teach the Bible and establish something there. Crickets. All they know how to do is slander.

sense.text:
Now into the topic: identifying Babylon. Many Christians say Babylon is Iraq. Ancient Babylon is in modern-day Iraq, about 50 miles south of Baghdad. A Christian apologist argued on the phone that Babylon the great is not the United States of America but ancient Iraq, and it was a waste of time: trying to convince a non-spiritual man to understand something spiritual.

“Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the spirit which is of God”: brothers, we have not received the spirit of the world; we’ve received the Holy Spirit, “that we might know the things that are freely given to us of God.”

“Which things also we speak, not in the words which man’s wisdom teacheth, but which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual.” We don’t teach in man’s wisdom of words. Comparing spiritual things with spiritual means precept upon precept, here a little and there a little.

“But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God”: the natural man is the sinful man, the so-called Christian man, the so-called Israelite man, even those not keeping the Commandments. “For they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.”

You must have the Holy Ghost on you to understand precepts in the Bible. Without it you’ll say, I don’t understand it, I cannot see it. That’s why a Christian can’t comprehend the slave ships, getting off the slave ship and sold to our enemies: no, that’s not what it means. What does it mean, then? I don’t know. Or Christ’s woolly hair and feet like they burned in a furnace: it means judgment, it don’t mean color.

precepts.why:
This verse is about Israelites, our people. “Why speakest thou unto them in parables?” Why do you speak to the people in dark sayings, in illustrated stories? “Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.”

Christ gave the apostles and the disciples an advantage over the other Israelites. Likewise you men, you sisters, have an advantage over the other Israelites who don’t know who they are, who are in Christianity, in Islam, and confused when they read the Bible.

Now Esau. Surely the white man knows: he reads manuscripts and textbooks, archaeological digs and ancient texts. “As for the mysteries of God, they knew them not.” The ungodly, the white man, knew them not.

Trying to debate or discuss something with an Edomite, he’s never going to agree with what you see in the Bible, so why waste your time, brothers? Some of y’all are in the comment boards arguing with scoffers. A scoffer will never believe what the Bible is saying: their whole objective is to disagree with you, with us, with God.

sense.text: This is for the Christians who say Babylon in the Bible is only talking about the time of Nebuchadnezzar. “And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.” Remember how God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah: with fire and brimstone.

“It shall never be inhabited, neither shall it be dwelt in from generation to generation: neither shall the Arabian pitch tent there; neither shall the shepherds make their fold there.” Babylon will never be inhabited. Is Iraq inhabited today, brothers? Yes: the pictures of Iraq today show it. So the Babylon of this prophecy is not Iraq. All these scoffers don’t understand the Bible.

“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city.” Who or what is this great city? Babylon the great, a.k.a. the United States of America. Their dead bodies are us: we are spiritually dead, and our dead bodies lie in the street of Babylon the great.

“Which spiritually is called Sodom”: when you’re on the street, emphasize the word spiritually, so the people will know this is a spiritual Babylon, not the literal Babylon. It’s called Sodom because America promotes same-sex marriage; this ain’t the real Sodom but a spiritual Sodom. “And Egypt”: this ain’t the real Egypt, but the same elements of ancient Sodom and ancient Egypt are here. That’s what God is letting us know.

“Where also our Lord was crucified”: our Lord was crucified in the land of Israel, just outside Jerusalem. This isn’t the real Jerusalem, but the elements of it are here: just like Christ was crucified there, here in America they crucify his image and his teachings.

precepts.why: Go a few chapters over and John tells you the name of this great city: “Babylon is fallen, is fallen, that great city, because she made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication.” So the great city where the dead bodies lie is Babylon the great, the United States of America.

The dead bodies: “We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes”, and we got eyes, “we stumble at noonday as in the night; we are in desolate places as dead men.” This is talking about our people, and see what it calls us: dead men.

Atlanta has dead men, New York City has dead men, Chicago, California has dead men, because we see with our eyes but can’t comprehend with our spirit.

sense.text: “I will shew unto thee the judgment of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters”: the symbol is the Statue of Liberty. She sits upon many waters because America has over 845 bases around the world. She’s everywhere; America is the police of the planet, and trying to go up into space and take that too.

“With whom the kings of the earth have committed fornication”: their policies, their politics, their religions. That’s spiritual fornication. Everyone is in bed with the United States of America, and if you’re not in bed with her, they put sanctions on you, an embargo on you: all the nations.

“And the inhabitants of the earth have been made drunk with the wine of her fornication”: with the lies of her policies.

“I saw a woman sit upon a scarlet coloured beast, full of names of blasphemy, having seven heads and ten horns.” The seven heads: Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia, Great Britain. The ten horns: Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Germany, the United Kingdom, Italy, Greece, France, Denmark and Ireland.

Scarlet means red, and it says red because it symbolizes a race of people. What race of people is red and hairy? Esau: that’s who it’s talking about.

“And the woman was arrayed in purple and scarlet colour, and decked with gold and precious stones and pearls”: she’s wealthy. “Having a golden cup in her hand full of abominations and filthiness of her fornication”: this goes with Revelation 13, the mark in the hand; it’s a precept for it. Sum it up in one word: sin.

“MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT.” Why does it say mystery? Because when you tell people America is Babylon the great, they say no, it’s Rome, it’s Rome, or Iraq: the two stupid answers you often hear. They say it can never be the United States of America, God bless America. That’s why it’s a mystery. “THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH”: America is a religious capital.

“And I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints, and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus.” This woman, Babylon the great, would murder the prophets. The saints are men and women; the martyrs of Jesus go into the prophets. A lot of our people are going to get jacked up. This ain’t come to pass yet, but it’s going to.
“Wherefore didst thou marvel?” Why are you shocked, why are you amazed, why couldn’t you understand? “I will tell thee the mystery of the woman”: that’s who you want to know.
